description: A street elevation study for a cannery-inspired commercial building in Sidney, BC — a composition of gabled storefronts stepping along the seaside high street, culminating in a tall corner block carrying the "Sidney Cannery" name, recalling the Saanich Canning Company that anchored the town's waterfront from 1904 to 1942.
The drawing survives in the family's archives. A cannery-style mixed-use building matching this character stands today at Beacon Avenue and First Street as part of the Sidney Waterfront Inn & Suites.
note: This page is a work in progress: the drawing is from the studio's archive, but the project's history — including whether the built Sidney building is this design — has not yet been confirmed.

image.alt: Sidney Cannery — hand-coloured street elevation of gabled storefronts and a corner cannery building
